overview: This file documents a 1949 effort by the U.S. occupation authorities in Japan to restore commercial wire telephone service between Japan and Korea over the submarine cable linking Fukuoka and Busan (then spelled Pusan). It contains the covering despatch from the United States Political Adviser for Japan, a diplomatic note forwarding the Japanese Government’s proposal, an interoffice check sheet recording Civil Communications Section and G-2 consideration, and a technical memorandum on the cable network’s wartime and postwar condition. The proposed “sender keep all” arrangement would allow each country to retain charges collected domestically, avoiding the absence of a workable exchange rate between the Japanese yen and Korean won; the documents also reveal plans for U.S. occupation censorship personnel to monitor approximately one quarter of non-privileged calls.

subfiles.title: Despatch No. 429 on reopening Japan–Korea telephone service
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser for Japan, Tokyo
subfiles.to: U.S. Department of State; copy to the American Embassy, Seoul
subfiles.about: The covering despatch transmits occupation-authority correspondence concerning the proposed restoration of commercial wire telephone service between Japan and Korea.
subfiles.summary: Despatch forwards Japan's proposal to reopen the Fukuoka-Pusan phone cable, with no military objection noted.

subfiles.title: Diplomatic note forwarding the Japanese telephone proposal
subfiles.from: Diplomatic Section, General Headquarters, Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.about: The Diplomatic Section formally forwards a Japanese proposal to reopen commercial telephone service between Fukuoka and Busan.
subfiles.summary: Note proposes reopening Japan-Korea phone service on a 'sender keep all' basis to avoid exchange-rate problems.

subfiles.title: CCS check sheet and G-2 concurrence on restoring the cable circuit
subfiles.from: Civil Communications Section (CCS), with endorsement by G-2 dated June 9, 1949
subfiles.to: Civil Section (CS), via G-2; endorsement returned to CCS via the Diplomatic Section
subfiles.about: An interoffice check sheet recommends referring the proposed Japan–Korea telephone arrangement to Korean authorities and records G-2’s approval.
subfiles.summary: Check sheet recommends 'sender keep all' terms for the Fukuoka-Pusan cable, with G-2 raising no objection.

subfiles.title: Memorandum on cable conditions, traffic, censorship, and regional circuits
subfiles.to: For the record; circulated between G-2 and the Civil Communications Section
subfiles.about: The memorandum reviews the condition and use of Japan–Korea telephone cables, proposed censorship coverage, and other surviving or defunct international cable routes.
subfiles.summary: Memo details the suspended Fukuoka-Busan phone circuit's wartime traffic and censorship, recommending a 25% monitoring rate on any reopened service.

interest: Shows postwar plans to reopen Japan-Korea telephone cables, balancing currency, censorship, and military concerns.
